elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: No professional/workmanlike standard appears in the rendered language; § 16.1(A) warrants only that M&I's systems "are capable of performing the Services in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement," which is a capability statement, not a standard-of-care warranty. The redline does not add one.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: § 16.1(B): "The reports made available to Customer shall be in substantial conformity with the customer bulletins and the User Manuals" — the deliverable outputs are warranted against the documentation.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: § 16.1(B) states no duration; it is a continuing obligation for the Term, but the Term length is not in the record, so a 12-month floor cannot be confirmed from the operative text supplied.
§ 16.1(A) is unqualified as to time and is not cut off by any sunset in the rendered text, so the Services warranty is not shorter than 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted subsection: "M&I shall promptly repair or replace the non-conforming Services or reports."
Inserted subsection: "or, at Customer's election, refund the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or reports."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the rendered § 16.1 language or in the insertion.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty appears in the rendered language or in the insertion.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: § 16.1(B) warrants substantial conformity of the reports made available to Customer with the customer bulletins and User Manuals, with no expiry stated, so it runs at least as long as any 90-day floor; the § 16.1(F) disclaimer is carved back by "EXCEPT AS SPECIFICALLY SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 16.1" and does not swallow it. The deterministic "period ≥ 90 days" check reads false only because no numeric period is stated; in substance an unexpiring warranty exceeds the floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: § 16.1(A) warrants M&I's systems are capable of performing the Services in accordance with the Agreement, with no time limitation, and survives the carve-back in § 16.1(F).

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted subsection expressly requires M&I to "promptly repair or replace the non-conforming Services or reports" for breach of the § 16.1 warranties; this fills the gap left by § 12.3, which offers only dispute resolution or termination plus Damages.
Inserted subsection: "at Customer's election, refund the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or reports."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the two duration floors are already satisfied by the untimed § 16.1(A) and (B) warranties (protected by the express carve-back in the § 16.1(F) disclaimer), and the single inserted subsection supplies the two missing remedy elements (repair/replace and refund).

The deterministic "warranty period ≥ 90 days" flag is a mechanical miss only: no numeric period is stated because the warranties are continuing rather than sunsetting, which is at least as favourable as a 90/30-day floor.

Preferred level fails on four elements the drafter did not press: no professional-and-workmanlike standard, no compliance-with-laws warranty, no malicious-code warranty, and no confirmable 12-month software conformance period. To reach preferred, add a standard-of-care sentence, a compliance-with-laws warranty, a no-malicious-code warranty, and an express 12-month software conformance period.

Minimality holds: nothing existing is deleted or paraphrased, the favourable § 16.1(F) carve-back and § 12.3 remedies are retained, and the insertion adds no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages categories, or procedure. Placing the refund at Customer's election (rather than Vendor's option) is a permissible allocation within the remedy elements and adds no requirement outside the fallback checklist.

Intent is preserved: the new subsection is an additional remedy for breach of the § 16.1 warranties, references only an existing section, leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict § 12.3 (non-exclusive) or the § 13.4 cap. Drafting nit only: the insertion should be lettered (e.g., § 16.1(G)) to sit cleanly in the existing A–F sequence.
